what: First adversarial review of pull request 5 of BRIEF-canon.md (the absorption shimmer; item 6). Three lenses, as RUN-canon.md sets the round: design and accessibility (the glow's placement on dino.jpg and art-unstoppable.jpg at both widths and in both themes, the art unchanged, the tile's place and the screen-reader tree, reduced motion), copy (every sentence on the changed views against the engine and each other, the cards, the README and the pull request), and code (the tally against the engine's runs, which drag figure feeds the shimmer, the floor and the steps taken from the ladder by key, the tests and their mutants). Reviewed at 1d92534 (the page stage, on the engine stage 3cb9f60). Each report was reproduced or refuted by a skeptic with its own script: 13 reports, which make 11 findings once two pairs are merged (design-unbounded-no-physical-answer and copy-3 are one defect seen by two lenses, fixed once; code-2 and code-3 are two faults in realAirThrow, fixed as one; each report is recorded under its own id): 9 confirmed and fixed, 2 refuted (design-flicker-word-vs-car-crash: canon's band, decision 14; copy-6: the ladder's rule, recorded in Known limits; neither changed). The major: copy-1, four page texts saying absorbed energy changes nothing, against canon's 'it shows'. Fixed as the session lead decided: with the skeptics' better fixes, except where an outcome says otherwise (code-2's rule extended to the toss's and the legs' flights that never come down, so one rule holds for all; the relativistic case kept at all of the energy and labelled an upper bound; copy-2 worded for Collide's moving charger); every figure worked out in the engine (at 1d92534 and after, scratchpad pr5/r1fix/js/figs.js) or read on the page, never copied by hand. No fix needed canon CLAUDE.md doesn't settle; the changed drag rule is in the owner's item 1 (README and description alike). Each fix was reverted on its own in a scratch copy and its check seen failing (scratchpad pr5/r1fix/js/revert1.py, results in pr5/r1fix/revert1-results.json: 17 reverts, 6 in the engine and 11 on the page and in the cards); the README and description fixes have copy checks (pr5/r1fix/js/docs1.py) that fail on the old text. The review's 6 page mutants and its control each fail a check now; of its 15 engine mutants 13 fail and 2 are equivalent (09 and 11); the engine stage's 53, re-run with 7 patterns followed into this round's code, give 52 failing and the one equivalent (nan-guard), as at that stage. With every power off every engine result is byte-identical (powers.js part 1, 162 s, its fixture unchanged). After the fixes, the full Rex lab test line, one test at a time in the 4-CPU cloud sandbox, and all pass: build-data.py and build.js; calibration.js all checks passed (105 s); presence.js 383 checks (49 s); shots.js 85 checks, no problems (863 s, was 806 s at 1d92534); powers.js 217 of 217 (232 s; section 9 now 36 checks, was 29); ladder.js 578 of 578 (1 s); sweep.js 7,776 contexts with no NaN or negative output (566 s). node test/shots.js --pr5 alone: 61 s before the fixes, 63 s and 68 s after (19 checks, was 13).
es_summary: 52 fail a check, the seven followed among them, and nan-guard survives: it removes one of the tally's two NaN guards, and the other (add() skips a falsy value) still keeps NaN out, so it is equivalent, as at the engine stage
